title: Case Study: Twitter / News Feed Design
summary: Design a highly available news feed supporting hundreds of millions of users, focusing on the hybrid fan-out on write vs fan-out on read architectures.

explanation.overview: A News Feed system collects status updates from people you follow and displays them in reverse chronological order. It is an extremely read-heavy system (often 100:1 read-to-write ratio). The core problem is the 'Celebrity Fan-out' issue: when an average user tweets, we can easily push it to their 50 followers. But when a celebrity heavily followed by 100 million people tweets, pushing it to all followers would completely melt the database.
explanation.how_it_works_internally: INTERNAL Mechanics: We use a Hybrid Fan-Out Architecture. Average Users use 'Fan-out on Write' (Push Model). When user A posts, a background worker instantly copies the tweet ID into the pre-computed redis cache timelines of all followers. Reads are O(1). Celebrities use 'Fan-out on Read' (Pull Model). When Justin Bieber tweets, we DO NOT push it. Instead, when a follower opens their app, the system checks the celebrity's recent tweets and merges it into the user's timeline on-the-fly.

step_by_step.title: API Design
step_by_step.detail: POST /v1/tweet (body: content, media_ids). GET /v1/feed (query: cursor). We exclusively use cursor-based pagination so that new tweets arriving do not shift the offset window and cause users to see duplicate tweets.

step_by_step.title: Data Modeling
step_by_step.detail: Tweet Table: ID, UserID, Content, CreatedAt. User Relation Table: FollowerID, FolloweeID. Timeline Cache (Redis): Key=UserID, Value=List<TweetID>.

step_by_step.title: Handling the Celebrity Problem
step_by_step.detail: A user is marked as a 'celebrity' when they cross 100,000 followers. The graph database triggers a bit flip. The Fan-out service now ignores them. The Read API is modified to always query the cached list of 'celebrities I follow' and merge their recent tweets via a K-Way Merge algorithm.

key_concepts.definition: INTERNAL: Pre-computing the feed during write time. Pros: Feed loading is instant. Cons: Massive write amplification. A single tweet by someone with 1M followers generates 1M database rows or cache updates.

INTERNAL: Computing the feed during read time (when the user requests it). Pros: Minimal storage, saves resources for inactive accounts. Cons: Feed generation is slow (high latency), vulnerable to thundering herds.

examples.title: Python Implementation Snippet: K-Way Feed Merge
examples.description: Concrete Python code using heaps to merge pre-computed feeds with celebrity pull feeds in O(N log K) time.
examples.code:
import heapq

def merge_feeds(my_cached_feed, celebrity_feeds):
    # my_cached_feed is a list of [timestamp, tweet_id]
    # celebrity_feeds is a list of lists of [timestamp, tweet_id]
    min_heap = []
    # Negate timestamp to simulate Max Heap in Python (newest first)
    for feed in [my_cached_feed] + celebrity_feeds:
        if feed:
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, (-feed[0][0], feed[0][1], feed, 0))
            
    merged_timeline = []
    while min_heap and len(merged_timeline) < 20:
        neg_ts, tweet_id, feed_list, idx = heapq.heappop(min_heap)
        merged_timeline.append(tweet_id)
        if idx + 1 < len(feed_list):
            next_item = feed_list[idx + 1]
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, (-next_item[0], next_item[1], feed_list, idx + 1))
    return merged_timeline

examples.title: Decision Matrix & Tradeoffs: WebSockets vs Long Polling
examples.description: Evaluating how to deliver new tweets live to the frontend.
examples.code:
OPTION WebSockets vs OPTION Server-Sent Events (SSE)
----------------------------------------------------
Pros WebSockets: Full duplex communication, real-time.
Cons WebSockets: Heavy, requires persistent stateful connections, hard over L7 Load Balancers.
Pros SSE: Native HTTP, easier to load balance, automatic reconnection.
Cons SSE: Unidirectional (server to client only). (SSE is preferred for feeds since clients just read).

examples.title: Failure Modes & Exception Handling
examples.code:
try-catch fallback mechanics:
1. RedisConnectionFailureException: If the timeline cache dies, users fallback to pulling from the RDBMS, which induces a Thundering Herd. Therefore, we implement robust rate limiting on the fallback path and use a Singleflight request pattern to collapse identical DB queries.

configurable_params.name: Library Configuration Parameters (Kafka Producer)
configurable_params.effect: Modify parameter `acks=all` for financial transactions, but for Twitter feed generation, `acks=1` (leader only) or `acks=0` is preferred for maximum throughput.
configurable_params.tradeoff: Losing a few feed update events is acceptable in a social network compared to the latency penalty of strict consistency.

advanced_tweaks.when_to_use: Scaling WebSocket connections for real-time live events (Superbowl).
advanced_tweaks.how: Stateful WebSocket servers maintain user connection state. Instead of saving IP state to a DB, use a Pub/Sub backbone (Redis Pub/Sub). When a tweet arrives, publish it to a Redis channel. The specific Stateful Server subscribed to that user pushes the update instantly.

diagram.description: Separation of Push (Normal Users) and Pull (Celebrities).

data.mermaid_source:
graph TD
  Client[Mobile Client] --> API[API Gateway]
  API --> |POST Tweet| WriteSvc[Tweet Write Service]
  WriteSvc --> DB[(Primary Postgres)]
  WriteSvc --> Kafka[Kafka Event Stream]
  Kafka --> Fanout[Fan-out Workers]
  Fanout --> GraphDB[(Graph DB: Check Followers)]
  Fanout --> |If Followers < 100k| PushRedis[(User Timeline Redis - PUSH)]
  
  API --> |GET Feed| ReadSvc[Feed Aggregator Service]
  ReadSvc --> PushRedis
  ReadSvc --> GraphDB2[(Graph DB: Get My Celebrities)]
  ReadSvc --> PullRedis[(Celebrity Timeline Redis - PULL)]
  PushRedis -.-> Merge[K-Way Merge Alg]
  PullRedis -.-> Merge
  Merge --> Client

limitations: Inactive Users: Fanning out to dead accounts wastes immense Redis RAM. TWEAK: Only fan-out to Users active in the last 14 days. If an inactive user logs in, synchronously generate their feed.
Timeline Truncation: Storing infinite timelines in memory crashes Redis. TWEAK: Set a strict LTRIM of 500-1000 items per user length. Older tweets require fetching from Cold Storage (Cassandra).

technologies_used.details: Acts as the literal timeline. `LPUSH` appends new tweets. `LRANGE 0 20` fetches the first page of the timeline. O(1) performance.
Used as the permanent cold storage for actual tweet content. Scalable infinitely by hashing the TweetID, distributing PBs of text/images seamlessly without manual sharding.
